# Java — understand the language and the runtime separately

The Java language defines types, methods, classes, generics and exceptions. The **JVM** executes bytecode, manages runtime memory and implements defined concurrency semantics. Both layers matter, but they answer different questions.

## 1. Object references are copied; objects are not

~~~java
public class Main {
    static class User { int age = 3; }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        User a = new User();
        User b = a;
        b.age = 7;
        System.out.println(a.age); // 7
    }
}
~~~

Both variables refer to one User object. Java passes method arguments by value: when the value is an object reference, the reference is copied. This is different from Rust moves and borrows.

## 2. Interfaces specify a capability

~~~java
public class Main {
    interface Named { String name(); }
    record User(String name) implements Named {}
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Named x = new User("Ada");
        System.out.println(x.name()); // Ada
    }
}
~~~

The record generates its constructor and accessor. The interface promises a method, not a particular class inheritance chain.

## 3. Generic types are mostly erased at runtime

~~~java
import java.util.List;
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        List<String> names = List.of("Ada");
        System.out.println(names.get(0)); // Ada
    }
}
~~~

The compiler verifies that this list is used as a list of String values; generic type arguments are generally erased from the runtime representation. Do not treat List<String> and List<Integer> as distinct JVM classes.

## 4. Checked exceptions and resources

~~~java
import java.io.StringReader;
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        try (StringReader r = new StringReader("A")) {
            System.out.println((char) r.read()); // A
        }
    }
}
~~~

Try-with-resources closes the resource deterministically even when the body throws; this is a distinct concept from waiting for garbage collection.

## 5. Concurrency begins with happens-before

A shared Java field read and written by different threads needs a **memory-model** explanation, not only an instruction-order explanation. Volatile publication, synchronized blocks and other synchronisation mechanisms create defined ordering guarantees.

For a single minimal runnable concurrency programme, follow the existing [JMM example](java/jvm/jmm/index.qmd). That specialised course covers read/write actions, visibility, data races, volatile, final-field publication and atomicity in depth.
